input: A shell-and-tube exchanger is used to heat cooling water as part of a refinery preheat train, and the performance of the exchanger is described by the figures that follow. The duty of the exchanger is 1467 kW. On the hot side, the stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C, while on the cold side the stream enters at 25 °C and leaves at 40 °C. The log-mean temperature difference for the exchanger works out at 121.7 K, and the installed area is 41.4 m2, which together give an overall coefficient of 291 W m-2 K-1. It is worth pointing out that fouling was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and that no cleaning cycle has been completed for this exchanger as yet, so the picture available in relation to fouling behaviour is necessarily a limited one, resting as it does on the experience of a single period of operation rather than on a comparison between the condition of the exchanger before and after any cleaning operation has been carried out on it. The coefficient that is reported should accordingly be understood as the coefficient of the exchanger in the condition in which it was assessed, and it would not be safe to assume that the same value would be obtained once the exchanger had been cleaned and returned to service in a clean condition, since the whole burden of the fouling observation is that the state of the surfaces is part of what the coefficient describes.
target: A shell-and-tube exchanger heats cooling water in a refinery preheat train. Duty is 1467 kW. Hot stream: 180 °C in, 130 °C out. Cold stream: 25 °C in, 40 °C out. The log-mean temperature difference is 121.7 K and the installed area is 41.4 m2, giving an overall coefficient of 291 W m-2 K-1. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run; no cleaning cycle has been completed. The coefficient therefore describes the exchanger as it stood over the assessed run, with the fouling that run represents and without a post-cleaning measurement for comparison. A cleaned exchanger would present a different coefficient, and the record contains no value for that state. The temperature programme fixes the driving force the stated area works against. The log-mean difference follows from the four terminal temperatures, and the duty, the area, and that difference together fix the coefficient: at the stated duty, an exchanger with less area would need a higher coefficient to close the same balance, and the installed area is the quantity that was actually provided. The single-run basis of the fouling assessment bounds what the passage can say about time. Fouling grows with service, the run covers one interval of that growth, and the coefficient over a longer interval, or after a cleaning cycle that resets the surface, stands outside the record. The passage therefore reports a working exchanger at a stated duty, in a stated fouling condition, on a stated temperature programme. It does not report a design point for a clean exchanger, and it does not report a fouling rate, because neither a clean measurement nor a second fouled measurement exists in the record against which such figures could be set.
